## Functional assignment

The 430-residue protein is most consistent with a **pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)-dependent kynureninase**, **EC 3.7.1.3**.

This assignment is supported by:

- Strong similarity to curated bacterial kynureninases: approximately **46–49% sequence identity** over most of the protein.
- Presence of an **Aminotran_5 PLP-dependent enzyme domain**.
- Presence of a C-terminal **KYNU_C kynureninase domain**.
- Homolog annotations identifying a catalytic PLP-linked lysine and kynureninase activity.

## Catalyzed reactions

The primary reaction is:

\[
\text{L-kynurenine} + \mathrm{H_2O}
\rightarrow
\text{anthranilate} + \text{L-alanine} + \mathrm{H^+}
\]

This corresponds to **Rhea RHEA:16813**.

The enzyme can also catalyze cleavage of 3-hydroxy-L-kynurenine:

\[
\text{3-hydroxy-L-kynurenine} + \mathrm{H_2O}
\rightarrow
\text{3-hydroxyanthranilate} + \text{L-alanine} + \mathrm{H^+}
\]

This corresponds to **Rhea RHEA:25143**.

## Cofactor and biochemical role

- **Cofactor:** pyridoxal 5′-phosphate (PLP)
- **Reaction type:** PLP-dependent carbon–carbon bond cleavage of kynurenine substrates
- **Likely biological roles:**  
  - degradation of L-kynurenine to anthranilate and alanine  
  - contribution to bacterial NAD⁺ biosynthesis through production of 3-hydroxyanthranilate-related intermediates

The reaction and enzyme family are strongly supported by curated homologs, but the exact substrate preference of this particular sequence remains a **homology-based prediction rather than a direct experimental result**.
